I’ll verify the Wikipedia perigee value and Kipchoge’s record marathon time, then calculate and round the travel time to the nearest 1000 hours.
First I’m checking the available knowledge base for any relevant source material before using public reference data.



Checking the knowledge base first; if it has no relevant entry, I’ll use Wikipedia/public web sources next.
```python
knowledge_result = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Moon minimum perigee value Wikipedia Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record pace", scope="session")
print(knowledge_result)
```

```python
knowledge_result = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Moon minimum perigee value Wikipedia Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record pace", scope="session")
print(knowledge_result)
```
```python
web_result = await web_search("Wikipedia Moon perigee minimum distance closest approach Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record time", max_results=5)
print(web_result)
```
```python
web_result = await web_search("Wikipedia Moon perigee minimum distance closest approach Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record time", max_results=5)
print(web_result)
```
I’ll now compute from the sourced values: 356400 km minimum perigee and Kipchoge’s 2:01:09 marathon record, using the marathon distance of 42.195 km.
```python
calculation = await calculator("(356400 / (42.195 / (2 + 1/60 + 9/3600))) / 1000")
print(calculation)
```
```python
source_check = await web_search("site:en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon minimum perigee 356400 km; Eliud Kipchoge 2:01:09 world record", max_results=5)
print(source_check)
```
17000 hours
